Approved minutes of the Troy School District Board of Education meeting held December 14, 2021 at the district Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Anne, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, and Wilson were present; Mr. Gottlieb was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Keyser, Young, and West. Approximately 35 members of the audience attended. In lieu of the Pledge of Allegiance, Mr. Schmidt asked those present to stand for a moment of silence and prayer to honor the students lost in the Oxford High School shooting and all those affected by the tragedy.

Recognition (TSD Mission Moment): The Board recognized the TSD Preschool for its inclusion program, in which students with special needs attend school alongside typically developing peers, integrating special education and related services throughout the program. Early Childhood Director Erin Keyser shared a video and introduced her team: Lauren DeGrazia (School Social Worker), Elizabeth Neuville (General Education Teacher), Katie Drinkard (Teacher Consultant), and Grace Lynch (Speech & Language Pathologist).

Additions & Deletions: Dr. Machesky noted that agenda item 10.A., a Legislative Report from State Representative Kuppa, was deleted because Representative Kuppa was out of the country due to a family emergency; the District and Board planned to meet with Senator McMorrow and Representative Kuppa in January 2022 for a legislative update.

Consent Agenda (Resolution 21-089): Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Dr. Wilson, the Board approved items A through G: corrected minutes of the October 19, 2021 meeting; minutes of the November 9, 2021 Workshop; minutes of the November 16, 2021 meeting; the Sex Education Advisory Board for 2021-2023; the October 2021 Treasurer's Report; Budget Amendment #1; and the Hill Coil & Condensing Unit Replacement. Vote: 6 yes, 0 no, Gottlieb absent.

Business - Roofing Replacement Program (Resolution 21-090): Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mrs. Hammond, the Board awarded roof-replacement bids as expenditures of the Capital Projects Fund and Building Site & Sinking Funds: JD Candler for Athens High School and Schroeder, $740,910.00; Royal West Roofing for Troy High School, $623,469.00; plus a 5% contingency of $68,218.95, for a total of $1,432,597.95. Vote: 6-0, Gottlieb absent.

Business - Construction, Windows & Doors at Barnard, Bemis & IAE (Resolution 21-091): Moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mr. Hauff, the Board awarded bid pack 33 as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund: Environmental Glass Inc. exterior doors, $567,000.00, plus a strategic change order of $70,000.00; Triangle Window Fashions, Inc. roller shades, $13,540.00; and an 8% contingency of $46,443.00, for a total recommended award of $696,983.00. Vote: 6-0, Gottlieb absent.

Business - Door Lock Hardware (Resolution 21-092): Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board approved purchasing Nightlock Lockdown hardware for $162,922.95 from Taylor Brothers Door Lock, LLC, as an expenditure of the General Fund, the 2019 Capital Projects Bond, and/or the Building Site & Sinking Fund. Vote: 6-0, Gottlieb absent.

A network firewall bid recommendation letter on Convergent Technology Partners letterhead (6197 Miller Road, Ste #4, Swartz Creek, MI 48473; 810.720.3820; info@ctpartners.net), dated January 26, 2022, addressed to Beth Soggs, Technology Director, Troy School District, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48084. The subject line reads "Network Firewall Bid #9938 Recommendation," though the body recommends award of Firewall Bid #9937.

Background: On December 10, 2021, Troy School District issued an RFP soliciting bids to replace the district's network firewall, which provides network security for students and staff district-wide. The RFP was posted to the district's website, the State of Michigan site, and USAC (for the E-rate application). On January 12, 2022, sealed bids were accepted and opened; three proposals were received, read, and recorded. Several mandatory and voluntary alternates were provided, but none were acceptable to the district for technical and financial reasons.

Initial base bids: Delta Networks $327,353.04; People Driven Technology (PDT) $322,336.36; CBI $247,367.00.

Evaluation: All proposals were evaluated for compliance with RFP requirements, pricing, technical solution, and acceptance of terms and conditions. CBI was found non-compliant because it bid a single-year solution when a 5-year product and support solution was required. The two remaining bids were compliant. During evaluation, the author found that People Driven Technology used a pricing model that made a large portion of its proposed solution ineligible under both the USAC E-rate program and bond funding. The E-rate program currently provides a 40% discount to TSD; because of PDT's pricing model, those items would have to be purchased through general funds. The financial comparison: Delta $327,353.04 base, all E-rate eligible, $0 ineligible, $196,411.82 total after discount, $0 general funds required; PDT $322,336.36 base, $151,936.23 eligible, $170,400.13 ineligible, $261,561.86 total after discount, $170,400.13 general funds required.

Recommendation: Award the Firewall Contract (Bid #9937) to Delta Networks, with a district-approved 5% contingency -- base bid $327,353.04, contingency $16,367.00, total award $343,720.69. Delta Networks has provided services to the district over the years and has a significant client base across Oakland, Wayne, and Macomb Counties, including both Rochester and Dearborn schools. The service is eligible for reimbursement under E-rate Category 2, with the district receiving approximately 40% of expenditures up to 40% of the approved base bid amount. This is agenda item 10.A (dated 02.15.22), presented under "OTHER" at the February 15, 2022 Regular Meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education. It offers a resolution in support of the federal IDEA Full Funding Act, with a recommended action to adopt the resolution, and includes "Moved by" and "Supported by" signature lines plus YES and NO vote-recording lines (left blank in the document).

Background: In March, members from the K-12 Alliance will meet with members of Congress in Washington, DC to advocate for full funding of the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA). Congress enacted IDEA in 1975 to ensure all students with disabilities have access to quality public education, committing to fund up to 40% of the additional cost schools would face to provide services. Today the federal investment in IDEA is less than 14%. The IDEA Full Funding Act of 2021 (HR 5984) would require yearly increases to IDEA program funding so that the federal government reaches an annual appropriation of 40% of the cost of special education services within the next 10 years, fulfilling the obligation made in 1975. The K-12 Alliance is asking school boards to pass resolutions in support.

The suggested resolution's WHEREAS clauses state: the Troy School District recognizes the need for a strong investment in IDEA; IDEA was first enacted in 1975 to help ensure a free appropriate public education for students with disabilities; with IDEA's enactment Congress committed to fund up to 40 percent of the additional cost of special education, thereby promising up to 40 percent of the national average per-pupil expenditure, currently estimated at $13,828 by the U.S. Department of Education; more than 45 years later, the current federal investment is less than 14 percent; the district and other public districts educate a growing number of children with disabilities, now more than seven million; districts face increased demand for greater resources, including for students with multiple disabilities whose individual education plans require more resources; and with each increase in the IDEA child count the Board and others adjust their budgets, with some districts dedicating forty percent or more of their general education budgets to special education services.

The resolution then resolves that the Troy School Board supports the IDEA Full Funding Act, which would strengthen the federal investment in special education by authorizing a ten-year plan to fully fund the federal share of IDEA; urges Congress' strong bipartisan support for and passage of the Act; and remains committed to providing students with disabilities and their families the supports they need, acknowledging the intergovernmental partnership among the local, state, and federal levels of government critical to this shared investment in the nation's children.

Foster, RCDD, President of Convergent Technology Partners (6197 Miller Road, Ste. 4, Swartz Creek, MI 48473), sent a recommendation letter to Beth Soggs, Technology Director of Troy School District (4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48084), regarding the network firewall replacement. Although the subject line references Bid #9938, the letter body and award recommendation identify the solicitation as Firewall Contract Bid #9937. The firewall provides network security for students and staff district-wide.

Troy School District issued the RFP on December 10, 2021, posting it to the district website, the State of Michigan site, and USAC for E-rate application. Sealed bids were accepted and opened on January 12, 2022, with three proposals received, read, and recorded. The base bids were: Delta Networks, $327,353.04; People Driven Technology (PDT), $322,336.36; and CBI, $247,367.00. Several mandatory and voluntary alternates were provided but none were acceptable for technical and financial reasons.

CBI was found non-compliant because it bid a single-year solution when a five-year product and support solution was required. The two remaining bids were compliant. During evaluation, Convergent found that PDT used a pricing model that made a large portion of its proposed solution ineligible under both the USAC E-rate program and bond funding; the E-rate program currently provides a 40% discount to TSD. A financial-impact table shows Delta's $327,353.04 base bid as fully E-rate eligible ($0 ineligible), yielding a total after discount of $196,411.82 with no general funds required, whereas PDT's $322,336.36 base bid was only $151,936.23 eligible and $170,400.13 ineligible, resulting in $261,561.86 after discount and $170,400.13 in required general funds.

Based on this evaluation, Convergent recommends awarding the Firewall Contract Bid #9937 to Delta Networks and that the district approve a 5% contingency. The award is stated as: base bid $327,353.04, contingency $16,367.00, total award $343,720.69. Delta Networks has provided services to the district over the years and has a significant client base throughout Oakland, Wayne, and Macomb Counties, including Rochester and Dearborn schools. The service is eligible for reimbursement under E-rate Category 2, with the district receiving approximately 40% of expenditures up to 40% of the approved base bid amount. Foster provided a contact number of 810-223-0528.

An internal Troy School District (TSD) email thread built around a K-12 Alliance of Michigan "Action Alert" concerning federal special-education funding.

Thread sequence: The original alert was sent Thursday, February 3, 2022 at 4:57 p.m. by Nicole Christian of Oakland Schools to the OCSA (Oakland County) listserv, forwarded on behalf of David Randels of Oakland Schools, and copied to OSCabinet, David Randels, and Lisa Hansknecht. On Monday, February 7, 2022 at 12:28 p.m., Superintendent Richard M. Machesky, Ed.D. (Office 248-823-4003) forwarded it to Board President Karl Schmidt, copying Judy Holmes, writing: "I would also recommend we discuss this on Thursday and prepare to have it on our February agenda." At 4:36 p.m. that day, Schmidt replied "okiedokie," signing as Troy Board of Education President.

Substance of the alert: In March, K-12 Alliance members would meet with members of Congress in Washington, DC to push for full funding of the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA). The alert recounts that when Congress enacted IDEA in 1975 to ensure students with disabilities have access to quality public education, it committed to fund up to 40 percent of the additional cost schools face to provide those services; today the federal investment is less than 14 percent. The IDEA Full Funding Act of 2021 (HR 5984) would require yearly increases so the federal government reaches an annual appropriation of 40% of the cost of special education within the next 10 years.

The call to action asks recipients to work with their school boards to pass resolutions supporting the Act; a sample "Sample School Board Resolution.docx" was provided. Passed resolutions were to be emailed to Katie Whitman-Herzer at katie@k12michigan.org, to be compiled and brought to Washington on March 10th to share with members of Congress. The alert is signed by Robert McCann, Executive Director, and Katie Whitman-Herzer, Administrative Director, of The K-12 Alliance of Michigan (P.O. Box 16085, Lansing, Michigan 48901).

The email also appended a "Media Clips" section linking Michigan education news items -- including stories on Betsy DeVos backing school-choice petitions, Governor Whitmer's tax-cut and school-funding positions, a bill to let college students lead classes amid teacher shortages, an Oxford High shooting lawsuit challenging governmental immunity, debates over returning to in-person learning, use of COVID-19 ESSER funds for tutoring and mental health, virtual local board meetings, districts running low on snow days, and outside money flowing into voter-ID and school initiatives.
